routes.label: Use the speed at which sound closes the gap

question: A powderman set a fuse for a blast to take place in \(30\) seconds. He ran away at a rate of \(8\) yards per second. Sound travels at the rate of \(1080\) feet per second. When the powderman heard the blast, he had run approximately:
solution:
The sound begins traveling when the blast occurs, after the powderman has already run for \(30\) seconds. First express both speeds in yards per second:
\[
1080\text{ ft/s}=360\text{ yd/s},
\]
since \(3\) feet equal \(1\) yard.

At the instant of the blast, the powderman's distance from it is
\[
8\cdot30=240\text{ yd}.
\]
He continues running while the sound catches up. Each second the sound travels \(360\) yards and he travels another \(8\) yards, so their gap decreases by \(352\) yards. The catch-up time is therefore
\[
\frac{240}{360-8}=\frac{15}{22}\text{ s}.
\]
His total running distance when he hears the blast is
\[
240+8\left(\frac{15}{22}\right)
=\frac{2700}{11}
\approx245.45\text{ yd}.
\]
Thus he has run approximately \(\boxed{245\text{ yd}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
